question: Some two years ago, the monitoring committee for the Garisenda Tower, a historical monument that symbolises Bologna, warned that the tower was at risk of collapse. Despite this, the works to stabilise the tower have not yet started and there would seem to be no transparent plan for putting them into operation.

The city is said to have spent millions on installing metal containers around the tower, but these are doing nothing to help steady it and exactly how and when this will be done remains uncertain. Meanwhile, Bologna City Council has failed to provide any clear information to the public, with a total lack of transparency.

Following the emergency, resources were allocated for restoring and securing the Garisenda Tower under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) – Mission 1, Component 3, ‘Tourism and Culture’ – which forms part of the NextGenerationEU programme.

Any delay or non-compliance by Bologna City Council in the implementation or reporting of projects financed by the NRRP-NextGenerationEU risks incurring the loss of the corresponding European funding, thus entailing economic damage not only to the city, but also to Italy, which is managing the implementation of the NRRP rigorously and responsibly. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission know what stage has been reached in the works on the Garisenda Tower?
Will it verify, in cooperation with the Italian authorities, that the EU funding for this is being used correctly by the Bologna City Council administration?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.12.2025) In line with Regulation (EU) 2021/2411, the financial contribution allocated to Italy under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) is disbursed if the milestones and targets set out in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision on the approval of the assessment of the Recovery and Resilience Plan for Italy (CID Annex) are satisfactorily fulfilled2.

The consolidation and restoration of the Garisenda Tower may be reported by Italy as part of the final target in the context of Investment 2.4: ‘Seismic safety in places of worship, restoration of “Fondo Edifici di Culto” (Fund for Religious Buildings) heritage, and shelter sites for works of art (Recovery Art)’.

The Commission has not yet assessed the fulfilment of the target against the requirements specified in the CID Annex, including compliance with the established timeline as Italy has not yet submitted the corresponding payment request.

Member States remain primarily responsible for the implementation of their Recovery and Resilience Plans as approved in the CID Annex, as well as for verifying that the financing provided has been properly used in accordance with all applicable rules.
